readme:
# SVDQuant 平滑、低秩与残差量化

实现 [SVDQuant v1 §4.2 Eq. (5)](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05007v1) 的数值核心：把激活离群值迁移到权重，保留高精度主导低秩分量，对残差分支做量化。

## 函数

采用 `x[B,M]`、`weight[M,N]`、正且有限的 `scale[M]`。未量化输出是 `x@weight`，与 PyTorch Linear 的转置权重布局不同。

1. `smooth_inputs(x,weight,scale)` 返回 `(xs,ws)`：`xs=x/scale`、`ws=scale[:,None]*weight`，应保持 `xs@ws=x@weight`。
2. `split_weight(weight,rank)` 返回 `(left[M,r],right[r,N],residual[M,N])`，`left@right` 为截断 SVD 的最佳 rank-r 近似，`residual=weight-left@right`。允许奇异向量符号及等价因子分解不同，覆盖 `rank=0` 和 `rank=min(M,N)`。
3. `svdquant_linear(x,weight,scale,rank,bits=4)`：先平滑，再分解**平滑后的权重**，计算：

$$Y=(\hat X L_1)L_2+Q(\hat X)Q(R).$$

低秩分支必须接收**未量化的平滑激活**；低比特分支量化的是残差 R，不能量化完整平滑权重。已提供 `fake_quantize`：每个张量共享 `s=max(abs(z))/(2^(bits-1)-1)`，`Q(z)=s*clamp(round(z/s),-qmax,qmax)`，中点取偶数，零张量输出零，`2<=bits<=8`。

starter 已提供校验和量化。输入为有限 CPU float32/float64，同 dtype/device，维度非空。保留 dtype/device 与输入值，兼容非连续输入。本题为推理数值接口，不考查 SVD/rounding 梯度。

## Toy 实验

T3 构造含一个 30 倍通道的合成激活，通过提交函数计算输出误差及奇异值曲线，比较直接 W4A4、仅平滑与 rank 0–6 双分支结果。这是 Figures 4–5 的**教学改编**：平滑系数已给定，只做一次 SVD；高精度分支使用输入浮点 dtype，不模拟硬件 FP16。不含模型权重、校准搜索、迭代细化、FP4 编码、整数内核或 Nunchaku 延迟复现。核心同时包括平滑、低秩、残差量化，不将单独 SVD 当作完整系统。
notes:
# 题解

按本题布局，激活通道除以 lambda，权重**行**乘以 lambda。截断 SVD 可取 `left=U[:,:r]*singular[:r]`、`right=Vh[:r]`，等价分解也可；先计算残差，再量化。Eq. (5) 的高精度支路接收 xs，低比特支路接收 Q(xs)。两支路都用量化激活，即使满秩也无法恢复精确线性输出。

## 来源与数值范围

[v1 §4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05007v1) 将平滑权重写作 `W diag(lambda)`，但其 W 定义为 `[M,N]`。该布局维度一致的式子是 `diag(lambda) W`，本题采用后者，并用非方阵测试避免转置歧义。输出遵守 Eq. (5)，测试比较因子乘积，不限定奇异向量符号。

[作者仓库](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/deepcompressor/)是校准与推理系统。本题独立实现给定平滑系数、一次 SVD，并将 Eq. (1) 固定为张量级对称整数 fake quantization；不模拟生产校准配置、低秩迭代细化、group/FP4 变体、存储打包或 Nunchaku 融合内核。CPU float32/float64 代表高精度支路，不能据此声称硬件加速或存储压缩。

受控离群值 toy 计算真实输出误差及残差奇异谱，仅展示选定矩阵；不保证任意输入增大 rank 后量化误差都单调下降。独立 oracle 使用已知旋转奇异向量与 Python 标量 rounding，覆盖 rank=0/满秩和零张量。四个 mutant 对应反向平滑、高精度激活被量化、完整权重被重复量化、遗漏奇异值。

en.title: SVDQuant Smoothing, Low-rank and Residual Quantization
en.readme:
# SVDQuant Smoothing, Low-rank and Residual Quantization

Implement the numerical core of [SVDQuant v1 §4.2, Eq. (5)](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05007v1). Move activation outliers into the weights, retain dominant weight components at high precision, and quantize only the residual branch.

## Functions

Use `x[B,M]`, `weight[M,N]`, positive finite `scale[M]`; the unquantized output is `x @ weight` (not PyTorch Linear's transposed-weight layout).

1. `smooth_inputs(x, weight, scale)` returns `(xs, ws)` with `xs=x/scale`, `ws=scale[:,None]*weight`. This preserves `xs@ws=x@weight`.
2. `split_weight(weight, rank)` returns `(left[M,r], right[r,N], residual[M,N])`. `left@right` is a best rank-r approximation from truncated SVD and `residual=weight-left@right`. Any singular-vector signs or equivalent factorization are accepted. Support `rank=0` and `rank=min(M,N)`.
3. `svdquant_linear(x, weight, scale, rank, bits=4)` first smooths, then splits the **smoothed** weight, and computes

$$Y=(\hat X L_1)L_2+Q(\hat X)Q(R).$$

The low-rank branch uses **unquantized smoothed activations**. Quantize residual R, not the full smoothed weight. The provided `fake_quantize` uses one scale per tensor: `s=max(abs(z))/(2^(bits-1)-1)`, `Q(z)=s*clamp(round(z/s),-qmax,qmax)`, round ties to even, and zero maps to zero. `2<=bits<=8`.

The starter provides validation and quantization. Inputs are finite CPU float32/float64 with matching dtype/device and nonempty dimensions. Preserve dtype/device, support strided inputs and do not modify inputs. This is an inference numerical contract; gradients through SVD/rounding are outside the exercise.

## Toy experiment

T3 creates synthetic activations with one 30x channel, then recomputes output errors and singular-value curves through your functions. Compare naive W4A4, smoothing only and the two-branch approximation at ranks 0–6. This is a **teaching adaptation** of Figures 4–5, using given smoothing scales and a one-shot SVD. High precision means the input float dtype here, rather than hardware FP16. No checkpoint, calibration search, iterative refinement, FP4 encoding, integer kernels or Nunchaku latency reproduction is included. This is more than an SVD task, but still a bounded numerical core of the complete system.
en.notes:
# Solution notes

With the stated matrix layout, scale input channels by `1/lambda` and weight **rows** by `lambda`. Truncated SVD may use `left=U[:,:r]*singular[:r]`, `right=Vh[:r]`; another equivalent factorization is fine. Preserve the residual before fake quantization. In Eq. (5) the high-precision path sees xs, while the low-bit path sees Q(xs). A quantized input in both paths would lose the benefit even at full rank.

## Source and numerical scope

[The v1 text in §4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05007v1) writes the transformed weight as `W diag(lambda)` despite defining W[M,N]. For that layout the dimensionally consistent identity is `diag(lambda) W`, used here. The test's nonsquare matrix prevents this transpose ambiguity from passing unnoticed. The output follows Eq. (5) and tests compare products rather than singular-vector signs.

The [author implementation](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/deepcompressor/) is a calibration and inference system. This exercise independently implements one-shot SVD with supplied smoothing, and chooses an explicit per-tensor symmetric integer fake quantizer from Eq. (1). It does not model the full production calibration configuration, iterative low-rank refinement, grouped/FP4 variants, storage packing or Nunchaku fused kernels. CPU float32/float64 stand in for the high-precision branch; no hardware speed or compression claim follows.

The controlled outlier toy measures actual output error and residual spectrum. It demonstrates one deliberately chosen matrix; increasing rank or applying SVDQuant is not guaranteed to improve every arbitrary quantized matrix monotonically. Independent tests use known rotated singular vectors and Python scalar rounding, including rank-zero/full-rank and zero tensors. Mutants target reversed smoothing, quantized high-precision activations, quantizing the full weight twice, and omitted singular values.
